image_description: A close-up underwater shot of a Rock Beauty fish (Holocanthus tricolor) partially hiding within a rocky crevice. The fish displays the characteristic black anterior body and head, transitioning to a golden-yellow posterior section. The eye is visible and large. The background consists of purple and pinkish coral or rock structures.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is completely occluded by the angle of the fish and the surrounding rock structure; teeth are impossible to resolve at this resolution.
The eye is clearly visible, large relative to the head, and reflects light appropriately, matching the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed disc-shaped body with compact proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although partially hidden, the visible profile shows a high-backed, laterally compressed shape consistent with angelfish/butterflyfish morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Striking gold and black coloration: anterior body and head black, posterior body and tail golden yellow with black margin.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The distinct demarcation between the black front half and yellow rear half is clearly visible and matches the taxonomic ground truth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Continuous dorsal fin with spiny anterior and soft-rayed posterior portions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is largely occluded by the overhanging rock/structure above the fish. Only a small portion might be hinted at, but structural details (spines vs rays) cannot be verified.
The ventral side of the fish is obscured by shadow and the substrate it is resting near/hiding in.
The caudal peduncle and the base of the tail are visible, showing the correct curvature and transition from the yellow body, consistent with a rounded tail shape.
